traps.excerpt: Interview P06 was entirely excluded due to severe research-method flaws, including leading questions and duplicate text, providing zero evidentiary support
While the phrasing in P02:t8 was templated across several transcripts, independent quotes from P01:t10 and P03:t10 confirm that high setup friction is rejected
Solo Student Households (out-of-target contrast; sample size: 1 interview: P07)
Retired Couples with Fixed Routines (in-target demographic, but no problem fit; sample size: 1 interview: P09)
A single stated claim of 30 euros per month from adjacent participant P08 was anchored to an isolated holiday spoilage incident and is excluded as an extreme outlier
A1 (Usability risk, Riskiest assumption): Households will reliably input and maintain an up-to-date fridge and pantry inventory
While weekly shoppers follow plans, households with irregular schedules abandon weekly planning apps and feel guilt when plans fall apart
The idea brief claim that dinner planning causes couples to argue is weakly supported, reported by only 1 of 5 in-target households (P02), while the broader friction is uncoordinated grocery shopping
The idea brief claim that existing recipe apps do not know what you already own is contradicted by FridgeChef and PantryGenie
The claim that meal-planning software is growing at 25% annually is unsupported because it conflates planning software with meal-kit delivery services and lacks a source
What is the objectively measured food waste and grocery spend over time, rather than self-reported estimates

criteria.justification: The brief structurally answers every required question with extensive detail, leaving no gaps in the research synthesis or analysis of the idea brief.
Claims are consistently anchored to specific citations. The brief meticulously distinguishes between observed behavior and stated intent while explicitly noting sample sizes and contradictions.
Conclusions perfectly match the evidence, avoiding definitive statements on unvalidated points like willingness to pay and acknowledging the limitations of the qualitative dataset.

The recommendation is clear and justified. The proposed tests are highly concrete, containing specific target segments, sample sizes, clear methodologies, measurable success metrics, and definitive decision thresholds tied to the riskiest assumptions.
The brief is exceptionally well-structured with clear headings, bolded summaries, and bulleted lists that make it highly readable and immediately actionable for product teams.
